name: moon_sun_clock
description: Proves the moon rides §14's warped sun clock. The moon_elevation expectations are pure geometry and depend on nothing but latitude/day/hour, but the moon_shadow_render ones track the SHIPPED PRESET's shadow-strength slider (CelestialSettingsMath.Presets.Cinematic.ShadowStrength, currently 0.8) because Patch_ShadowStrength multiplies every shadow alpha by it. Recompute after a preset change: rendered = 1 - MoonShadowStrength * ShadowStrength * (1 - 0.107), where 0.107 is MoonMath.MoonShadowColorValue(0.25, 0.28) — §6a's night shadow colour, which a preset does NOT move.
_comment: Proves the moon rides §14's warped sun clock rather than the raw one. Latitude 45 / day 37 is
chosen because the moon is exactly full at noon there (tick-derived cycle 0.5000, so the
scenario is not silently testing a gibbous moon) and vanilla's day is 18.06 h against our
physical 14.61 h — a 1.7 h clock gap at each horizon, the largest an ordinary colony sees.
Vanilla's sunset lands at hour 21.03 and sunrise at 2.97.
Every expected value below was computed offline from the same pure cores the mod runs
(MoonMath + SunClockMath + Formulas), including the moon's phase drift across the day.
moon_clock_warp false reproduces the artifact §14 shipped with: sun warped, moon left raw.

steps._comment: Guard against a vacuous run: if this is not a full moon, nothing below means anything.
Midnight is a fixed point of the warp, so both clocks must agree exactly here. This is the control: it proves the change is a time warp and not a blanket offset applied to the moon.
An hour before vanilla's sunset, sun still 7.4 degrees up. On the raw clock the full moon is already in a lit sky; on the warped clock it is still below the horizon, where it belongs.

Hour 21.0 is still 2 minutes BEFORE vanilla's sunset (21.032), so the sun branch of both shadow patches still owns the shadow and moon_shadow_render reads ~0.995 on either clock. Probed deliberately: it fixes which side of the handoff we are on, and a moon-clock change must NOT move it.

Hour 21.1 — the first sampled moment PAST vanilla's sunset, so the sun shadow has just reached zero and the moon branch takes over. This USED TO BE the pop: on the raw clock the moon was already 13.6 degrees up, so the shadow snapped straight to full strength and the render dropped to 0.801 in one step.
steps._comment2: §6b RE-BASELINE. Both readings are now 1.0, and for a reason that has nothing to do with the clock: moon shadow strength is the moonlight-to-skylight ratio, and the sky here is still ~92 lux against the full moon's 0.27. No moon, at any elevation, casts a visible shadow at this moment. That is why the raw-clock pin moved 0.801 -> 1.0 while the warped-clock pin did not move at all. The moon_elevation probes below are what still separate the two clocks; the render probes have become a §6b guard (if either reads ~0.80 again, the sun-below-horizon gate is back). See moon_shadow_twilight_fade.json for where the shadow actually arrives.

steps._comment: Hour 21.3. Pre-§6b this was 'mid-ramp': the warped moon 1 degree up, shadow fading in at render 0.881 while the raw clock had been saturated for 20 minutes — the continuity argument for warping the moon. §6b removed the ramp this was measuring. The sky is still ~8.9 lux, ~33x the full moon, so neither clock casts anything and both read 1.0. The moon_elevation probe is what carries the clock claim now.
Just after vanilla's sunrise (2.97). Raw clock leaves the full moon 8.8 degrees up in the morning sky; warped puts it below the horizon.
Deep night, both clocks. The fix must not have simply deleted the moon: it is well up and casting on the warped clock too, so the night stays moonlit.
§14's own contract is untouched by this change: vanilla's sky and our sun still agree about day/night at every hour.
